newsitem.title: USA: No policy problems from sweep accounts - Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: No policy problems from sweep accounts - Greenspan.

text.p: The Federal Reserve has experienced no difficulties in carrying out monetary policy due to banks' use of retail "sweep" accounts, Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan said Wednesday.

Responding to a question from the Senate Banking Committee during his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, the Fed Chairman said the effects of the use of sweep accounts by banks to avoid loss of interest due to reserve requirements was purely a technical issue.

"We have not felt ... any specific problem in implementing monetary policy," Greenspan said, adding that if problems were to arise in the Fed's ability to affect bank reserve positions, there are many other alternative methods of policy implementation that the central bank could use and obtain the same results it does now.
